title: Credit Controller
description:
As a Credit Controller in Wrexham, you will manage customer accounts within the Industrial / Manufacturing sector, helping the finance function keep records accurate and payments on track. You will handle day-to-day credit control work and provide clear account information that helps the business run smoothly.

Client Details

The organisation operates in the Industrial & Manufacturing sector in Wrexham. They are fairly well known in the area and have a strong reputation.

Description
- Manage a portfolio of customer accounts and maintain accurate account records.
- Contact customers to follow up on outstanding payments and agree practical next steps.
- Review aged debt reports and prioritise accounts that need timely action.
- Investigate payment queries and work with relevant colleagues to resolve them.
- Keep clear notes of customer contact, payment promises and account updates.
- Issue customer statements and provide information on account balances when needed.
- Reconcile customer payments against invoices to keep records up to date.
- Share regular debt updates with the Accounting & Finance department to support informed decisions.

Profile

A successful Credit Controller should have:
- Experience managing customer accounts and following up overdue payments.
- Confidence reviewing account balances, invoices and payment information.
- Ability to investigate payment queries and keep account records accurate.
- Clear written and verbal communication when dealing with customers.
- Good attention to detail when recording payment activity and account updates.
- Ability to organise workload and prioritise outstanding debt effectively.

Job Offer
- Permanent Credit Controller position based in Wrexham.
- Salary of 27,000 to 33,000, dependent on the level of experience.
- Excellent benefits package including enhanced pension and private healthcare.
- Really accessible location with plenty of free parking on site and close to local public transport routes.
- Full time role - 37.5 hours per week.

If you're interested in this role, apply now.

description:
Credit Controller (Part-Time)

Wrexham Hybrid Working 20 Hours Per Week 12-Month Contract

We're working with a growing and successful business based in Wrexham that is looking to add a Debtors Clerk to its finance team on a part-time basis.

This is an excellent opportunity for someone who enjoys building relationships, keeping accounts on track, and playing a key role in maintaining healthy cash flow. You'll be joining a supportive team where your contribution will make a real difference to the business.

- Issuing invoices, statements and payment reminders
- Following up on overdue accounts and maintaining accurate collection records
- Reconciling customer accounts and resolving payment queries
- Processing and allocating incoming payments
- Producing aged debt reports and supporting cash flow activities
- Building positive relationships with customers while ensuring payments are received on time
- Managing customer credit limits
- Processing credit notes and account adjustments
- Handling prepayments and releasing orders where required
- Completing online payment reconciliations

What We're Looking For
- Previous experience within credit control, debt recovery, or accounts receivable
- Strong attention to detail and excellent record-keeping skills
- Good problem-solving abilities and a practical approach to resolving issues
- Intermediate Microsoft Excel skills, including formulas, lookups and pivot tables
- Confident communication skills, both written and verbal
- Ability to manage your workload independently and prioritise effectively

Desirable Experience
- At least 12 months' experience in a similar role
- Experience using ERP or finance systems
- A good understanding of the full debtor management process

Working Hours

20 hours per week across 5 days, worked flexibly:
- Monday to Thursday between 9:00am and 5:00pm
- Friday between 8:00am and 4:00pm

Contract
- Initial 12-month contract
- Potential for extension or a permanent opportunity

What's In It For You?
- 28 days holiday, including bank holidays (pro rata)
- Company pension scheme
- Private healthcare support
- Free annual eye test voucher
- Free annual flu jab
- Mental health and wellbeing support
- Regular social and team events
- Free on-site parking
- Supportive and collaborative working environment
- Hybrid working with a minimum of two office days per week

Salary

Competitive salary available upon application.

This is an excellent opportunity for someone who enjoys taking ownership of their workload, has strong organisational skills and can confidently manage multiple priorities in a busy office environment.

Client Liaison & Contract Administration

Support managers with scheduling and work coordination.

Confirm work schedules and keep clients updated on any changes.
Maintain accurate contract records, visit schedules and client information.
Prepare and issue correspondence, reports and supporting documentation.
Record and track customer enquiries, concerns and complaints, ensuring appropriate follow-up.
Job, Supplier & Subcontractor Administration
Create and maintain customer, site and job records.
Log enquiries and support the quotation process.
Follow up on outstanding quotations and client responses.
Raise purchase orders and coordinate supplier deliveries.

Ensure all completed job records, photographs and paperwork are received and filed correctly.
Prepare documentation to support invoicing and resolve related administrative queries.
Office & Business Support
Manage incoming telephone calls, emails and correspondence.
Maintain electronic filing systems, spreadsheets, diaries and action trackers.
Monitor contract, insurance and company renewal dates.
Assist with audits, assessments and accreditation requirements.
Maintain company policies, procedures and compliance records.
Support employee administration, including onboarding paperwork, training records and timesheets.
Arrange meetings, prepare documentation and record actions where required.
Order office supplies and provide general administrative support to the leadership team.

Previous experience within a busy office administration role.
Excellent organisational skills and strong attention to detail.

Ability to work independently and use initiative.

Professional and confidential approach when handling sensitive information.
Desirable Experience
Contract administration experience.
Purchasing or supplier coordination experience.
Compliance or accreditation administration.
Employee administration, training records or payroll support.
Experience working within construction, grounds maintenance, engineering or field-based service environments.

WE RE RECRUITING!
Receptionist
Location: Corwen

Be the welcoming face of our community!
Do you enjoy meeting people, helping others and keeping things organised? SDCP is seeking a friendly, professional and organised Receptionist to welcome visitors and help our busy community centre run smoothly.
Your responsibilities will include
- Welcome visitors and respond to telephone and face-to-face enquiries.
- Manage bookings and routine administration.
- Maintain accurate records and handle correspondence.
- Process payments, receipts and basic cash transactions.
- Support colleagues, volunteers and community activities.
- Help keep the Centre safe, welcoming and efficient.

What we re looking for
- Excellent communication and interpersonal skills.
- Friendly, approachable and professional manner.
- Good organisational and administrative abilities.
- Confidence using computers and Microsoft Office.
- Accuracy, discretion and ability to manage competing priorities.
- Positive, flexible approach to teamwork.

Previous reception, administration or customer service experience would be an advantage.
Benefits: 20 days annual leave plus 8 public holidays and a 3% employer pension contribution.
Appointment is subject to relevant safeguarding and recruitment checks.
How to apply
For the full job description, application details and all recruitment enquiries, please contact Jobs in Wales. All applications must be submitted through Jobs in Wales.
Interviews: Wednesday 9 December 2026
Closing date: Friday 13 November 2026
SDCP is an Equal Opportunities Employer and welcomes applications from all sections of the community. Reasonable adjustments are available for disabled applicants.
Reports to: Centre & Transport Co-ordinator / Operations Manager or designated senior manager
Location: Predominantly Centre-based in Corwen, although flexibility to provide cover for external events is essential.
Purpose of Role
To provide a professional, welcoming and efficient reception and administrative service, ensuring that visitors, service users, staff, volunteers and callers receive appropriate support and information. The Receptionist helps maintain accurate records, supports bookings and payments, and contributes to the safe, organised and community-focused operation of the Centre.
Flexibility, Teamwork and Staff Cover
As part of a busy community centre, all staff are expected to work collaboratively and respond flexibly to changing service needs and priorities. The postholder will provide reasonable cover for colleagues and assist with other duties during busy periods, annual leave and sickness absence, as agreed with their line manager.
Cover duties will be appropriate to the postholder s skills, competence and level of responsibility, with any necessary training, guidance and support provided. Staff are expected to communicate promptly where competing priorities or capacity may affect their ability to provide cover, so that workloads can be agreed and services maintained safely and effectively.
Overall Accountability
To manage the day-to-day reception function, communications, routine administration, bookings, payments and visitor support in accordance with organisational procedures, while maintaining confidentiality, accuracy, professionalism and a high standard of customer service.
EMPLOYMENT CONDITIONS
Employer Pension Contribution: 3% employer pension contribution.
Annual Leave Entitlement:
- 20 days annual leave per annum plus 8 public holidays, based on a full-time, five-day working week, pro rata for other working patterns and part-year service.
- Upon completion of 3 years continuous service, you will be entitled to an additional day s annual leave for each completed year of service up to a maximum of 5 additional days after 8 years continuous service. The additional entitlement will be awarded from the start of the holiday year following completion of 3 years continuous service.

Employer: South Denbighshire Community Partnership
Additional / Prerequisite Conditions
Integrity, reliability, discretion and adaptability, with the ability to remain calm under pressure.
Clear, professional communication and customer service, including respectful and empathetic contact with people from diverse backgrounds.
Accurate administration and record keeping, with Microsoft Office / IT skills.
KEY AREAS OF RESPONSIBILITY
Key Responsibilities
Reception and telephone management; welcoming visitors; handling enquiries; post and messages; room bookings; records and data entry; payments, receipts and petty cash; centre supplies and presentation; food safety checks; support for community activities; and compliance with GDPR, safeguarding, health and safety and security procedures.
Payment processing: Receive and handle cash payments, and process card payments through SDCP s automated payment system. Record transactions and receipts accurately, follow cash-handling and reconciliation procedures, report discrepancies promptly, and safeguard customer and payment information.
Other organisational duties: Provide appropriate assistance with community services and activities, which may include one-to-one contact with vulnerable people, subject to training, safeguarding procedures, risk assessment and management authorisation.
Communication & Service
Act as a positive first point of contact. Communicate clearly and respectfully with people from diverse backgrounds, listen carefully to enquiries, use empathy and discretion, and ensure matters are passed to the appropriate colleague.
Confidentiality & Safeguarding
Protect confidential and personal information, follow GDPR and safeguarding procedures, and promptly report concerns or incidents through the appropriate channels.
The successful applicant will be required to undertake a satisfactory Enhanced DBS check, including the relevant barred list check(s) where applicable, in accordance with the responsibilities of the role. This requirement applies to any additional duties or staff cover undertaken where such checks are required.
Before requesting any barred-list information, SDCP must confirm and document the statutory eligibility of the post against the actual duties and applicable regulated-activity criteria.
DETAILED JOB DESCRIPTION
Decision Making: Deal with routine enquiries and administrative matters within agreed procedures and delegated authority. Escalate complaints, safeguarding concerns, financial discrepancies, safety issues and matters outside the role's authority.
Key Working Relationships: Centre & Transport Co-ordinator; Operations Manager; Chief Officer; staff and volunteers; transport drivers and booking staff; service users; visitors; suppliers; community partners and other organisations using the Centre.
Team Working: Work collaboratively with colleagues, communicate changing priorities and support service continuity in line with the Flexibility, Teamwork and Staff Cover clause above.
Skills & systems
Essential
Clear communication; accurate administration and record keeping; Microsoft Office / IT skills; practical problem solving.
Ability to handle cash securely, use an automated card-payment system, maintain accurate transaction records and report discrepancies.
Desirable
Experience of booking, payment, cash-handling or similar reception systems.
Customer service
Essential
Professional telephone and face-to-face customer service; ability to deal respectfully and empathetically with people from diverse backgrounds.
Desirable
Experience in a community, voluntary or public-facing service.
Organisation & accuracy
Essential
Ability to organise and prioritise work, maintain accurate records and handle information and money securely.
Desirable
Experience of working in a busy reception or administrative environment.
Teamwork & personal qualities
Essential
Team player; integrity; reliability; professionalism; empathy; patience; discretion; adaptability; positive attitude; ability to remain calm under pressure.
Special requirements
Essential
Commitment to confidentiality, safeguarding, GDPR, health and safety and inclusive service delivery. Appointment is subject to a satisfactory Enhanced DBS check, subject to confirmation of the role s eligibility (see Confidentiality & Safeguarding).
Driving licence (desirable only). title: Operations & Fulfilment Coordinator (Part Time)
description:
Job Description Operations Coordinator

Role at a glance

Hours:- 24 Hours per week, three full days, or spread across Monday to Friday by agreement

Location:- Flint, Mainly on site, with scope for some hybrid working once established

Salary:- £15.25 p/h

Contract:- Permanent, Part Time

About us

We are a small team where everyone's work matters and good ideas are acted on quickly.

The role

This is a hands-on role that combines purchasing, order administration and warehouse work. You will make sure customer orders are bought in, checked, packed and dispatched correctly and on time.

Over time you will take ownership of the day-to-day operational work currently handled by the Director, so that problems are picked up and solved without needing to be escalated.

For the successful candidate there will be growth opportunities.

Key responsibilities

Purchasing
- Raise purchase orders from the sales orders and check them for accuracy.
- Send purchase orders to our manufacturers with the required due dates.
- Check order confirmations against the dates and prices. Chase corrections where needed and update the system.
- Keep prices on purchase orders accurate and up to date.

Sales orders and dispatch
- Liaise with customers on product specifications and order details, working with the Directors where needed.
- Adjust and finalise sales orders so they are correct and ready to invoice before dispatch.

Warehouse
- Handle goods in and goods out.
- Carry out quality checks, pack orders for dispatch.

Technical support
- Help with pre-wiring of equipment. Training will be given.
- Cover warehouse and technical tasks during colleagues' holidays.

Continuous improvement
- Follow our established processes accurately.
- Look for better ways of working and suggest improvements. Good ideas will become part of how we work.

About you

Essential
- At least 2 years' experience in a similar role, such as purchasing, order processing, operations or warehouse coordination.
- A proven track record of solving problems and getting things right first time.
- Experience improving or correcting working procedures.
- A practical, hands-on approach, and happy to move between desk work and the warehouse.
- Sound judgement and the confidence to make sensible decisions without constant supervision.
- Strong attention to detail, especially with dates, prices and order information.
- Confident using computers, order or stock systems, and email.
- Open to trying new ways of working, and able to challenge existing methods constructively.

Desirable
- Experience with Unleashed or a similar ERP system.
- Knowledge of electrical or engineering sector.
- Forklift licence, or willing to train.

What we offer
- £15.25 per hour for 24 hours per week.
- Flexible hours pattern: three full days, or shorter days across the week.
- Scope for some hybrid working once you are established.
- Training in our products, systems and processes, including pre-wiring.
- A varied role in a small team where your ideas shape how the business runs.
- Workplace pension.
